question: Paryushana festival is celebrated by the people of which of the following communities?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Paryushana is one of the most important religious festivals celebrated by the Jain community.
 
• The festival lasts for 8 days for the Svetambara sect and 10 days for the Digambara sect.
 
• The word "Paryushana" means "to stay in one place," signifying a time of increased religious observance.
 
• It is marked by fasting, prayer, meditation, and introspection to purify oneself and seek forgiveness for past wrongs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jainism:**

 
 
• Jainism is one of the oldest religions in the world, originating in India around the 6th century BCE.
 
• The religion emphasizes non-violence (ahimsa), truth (satya), and asceticism as key principles.
 
• Jains believe in the cycle of reincarnation and the ultimate goal of achieving liberation (moksha) from the cycle of birth and death.
 
• The two major sects within Jainism are Svetambara and Digambara, each with its own unique practices and traditions.
 
 
 
• **Paryushana Festival:**
 
 
• Paryushana is considered a time for spiritual rejuvenation, involving rigorous fasting and self-discipline.
 
• During Paryushana, Jains engage in various religious activities such as reading scriptures, attending sermons, and participating in communal prayers.
 
• The festival concludes with the celebration of Kshamavani, or "Forgiveness Day," where Jains seek forgiveness from others for any harm or hurt caused intentionally or unintentionally.
 
• It is a time for Jains to reflect on their actions, repent for their sins, and make a renewed commitment to living a virtuous life.
